name: Aurora
description: Magnetospheric plasma intelligence manifesting as charged particle cascades along magnetic field lines, converting solar wind energy into luminous atmospheric patterns.

core_attributes.pattern: magnetospheric channeling, particle cascade, photon emission

scope.definition: Fraction of solar wind particle kinetic energy transferred to upper atmosphere (thermosphere) during geomagnetic storm via aurora borealis currents — measured by satellite energy balance studies.

evidence.source: Thayer & Semeter (2004) 'The convergence of magnetospheric energy flux in the polar thermosphere', Journal of Atmospheric and Solar-Terrestrial Physics 66:807-824.
cross_domain_examples: major geomagnetic storm (Kp=8): 10¹¹-10¹² W deposited in auroral zones — equivalent to 100 nuclear power plants
auroral electron precipitation: 0.85-0.95 of precipitated particle energy converted to atmospheric heat and optical emission
Joule heating accounts for 60-70% of total aurora energy deposition — larger than particle impact ionization

scope.falsifiability: If energy balance studies show aurora deposits <50% of estimated solar wind input to the magnetosphere, the remaining energy must be stored in ring current or tail regions — not dissipated.
scope.measurement_limits: Energy dissipation fractions are derived from model-data comparisons, not direct calorimetric measurement. Satellite constellation coverage gaps introduce systematic uncertainty of ±25%.
